sections.heading: C — Your License to Drive
sections.markdown:
## C — Your License to Drive

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Texas licenses cover residents, ninety-day new residents, non-farm commercial-free machines, sixteen-plus nonresidents for Class C or M, eighteen-plus nonresidents for anything with home reciprocity, and military drivers on home licenses with Texas cards surviving service plus ninety days [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Learner driving needs a sober watchful companion twenty-one plus with a year of experience, applicants run fifteen to eighteen with classroom education and exams passed, cards cost sixteen dollars total to age eighteen, practicing adults pay thirty-three dollars total for eight restricted years, and all prior cards surrender first [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A02
Under-eighteen first-timers file a school VOE proving a diploma, eighty prior-term days, or forty-five equivalency-prep days, fresh within thirty days in session or ninety in summer [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A02
Hardship licenses aid fifteen- to eighteen-year-olds via in-person adult petitions, full education and exams, and approval only for money crisis, family emergency, vocational need, or court order, inside a graduated system forcing driving exams on all newcomers, six learner months stretched by suspensions, and no Phase One wait for Class M [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A03
Phase Two caps young non-family passengers at one, bans midnight-to-five driving outside work, school, or emergency, and forbids under-eighteen wireless use beyond emergencies [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A03
PROVISIONAL cards run sixteen to eighteen after education, exams, and six learner months, out-of-state teens sort into Phase One or Two by credential, under-twenty-one cards read UNDER twenty-one, adult licenses run eight years for thirty-three dollars total with shorter special terms, and eight commercial-exempt vehicle types still need Class A or B [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A04
Class A spans B and C vehicles plus heavy combinations towing over ten thousand pounds and Class B spans C vehicles plus heavy singles towing ten thousand or twenty-thousand-pound farm trailers, neither touching motorcycles, each thirty-three dollars total for eight adult years with education through twenty-four or sixteen dollars total at seventeen with education [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A04
Class C covers lighter vehicles, small trailers and certified three-wheel autocycles, never motorcycles. Listed totals are $33 for adults, $16 at sixteen with approved driver education, or $6 at fifteen with hardship approval. Class M requires passing a state-approved motorcycle course; under-eighteen enrollees may show classroom-phase completion, a learner license or a valid Class C license as alternatives [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A05
Motorcycle licensing opens at sixteen after thirty-two plus sixteen hours or fifteen for small bikes via hardship or courses, charging thirty-three dollars total adult, sixteen dollars total young, sixteen to append, and twelve extra at renewal, with sixty-percent-plus disabled veterans skipping fees outside commercial and registrant cases [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A05
ID cards issue at any age, orient vertical under twenty-one, cost sixteen dollars total for six years through fifty-nine or six dollars total later, and backs allow two emergency contacts with allergy drugs handwritten since DPS prints no medical facts [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A06
Donor cards show a heart plus donor as conclusive consent, applicants may fund blindness care, Donate Life, veterans, evidence testing, or youth fees, filing happens in person with voter offers from seventeen years ten months, and men eighteen to twenty-five join selective service automatically [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A06
Applicants provide identity, Social Security number, fingerprints, medical-status/history answers and citizenship or lawful-presence proof, and surrender any valid out-of-state license. Exams, moving-traffic convictions and crashes enter the permanent record. Original applicants show Texas-minimum insurance for owned vehicles needing coverage, or state that none require it [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A07
New residents register all owned vehicles, fees with a one-dollar admin charge precede exams with none by mail, under-twenty-five drivers finish education, everyone finishes Impact Texas Drivers pre-exam, and under-eighteen filings carry a guardian oath signature cancellable before eighteen [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A07
Failures park applications ninety days, valid-license adults skip exams, passers earn forty-five-day temporary cards, knowledge exams span Class C originals, waivable Class M, and Class A and B rules with seventy percent passing all, and vision checks can mandate lenses or doctor visits [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A08
Driving exams follow passed exams and proven insurance in class-matched vehicles, excuse nobody under eighteen, run at offices and schools, skip learners, cost ten dollars to upgrade or fifteen to append M, and fail lawbreakers, the disobedient, the dangerous, and anyone beyond thirty lost points [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A08
Grading covers control, observation, positioning, signaling, parking, quick stops, backing, signs, signals, clutch, intersections, turns, right-of-way, following, passing, lanes, and posture, allowing cameras while banning automated parking [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A09
Failed exams reschedule, passers carry the license for officers and crash counterparts, unlicensed fines run two hundred dollars first and twenty-five to two hundred second within a year or Class A jail for deadly uninsured crashes, and restrictions change at any office [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A09
Duplicates and address moves cost eleven dollars total with thirty-day reporting, ten dollars by mail, other changes in person, no remote service for special licenses, and renewal notices stay pure courtesy [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A10
Renewal runs eight years with office visits each sixteen for vision and biometrics, remote service bars troubled, commercial, restricted, registrant, older, undocumented, and non-citizen filers, medical answers may reach the board, service families renew exam-free within ninety days of discharge, and out-of-state Texans mail fees and vision results to the printed date or ninety days after return [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A10
$100 may be required for mandatory suspensions, revocations and certain fraudulent-government-record convictions; drug-education reinstatement is $100. ALR reinstatement is $125. Some mandatory suspensions need SR-22. Listed automatic-suspension triggers include DWI, drug offenses, intoxication manslaughter and intoxication assault [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A11
Automatic suspension adds aid failures, deadly crashes, felonies, bus repeats, boating intoxication, evading, invalid driving, card fraud, graffiti, fake plates, false records, and racing [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A11
Hearings suspend for bad patterns of four convictions in twelve months or seven in twenty-four plus exam and probation failures, and under-twenty-one drivers fall automatically for alcohol, tobacco-class, drug, and Chapter four eighty-one offenses [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A12
After a proper hearing, a minor may face suspension or revocation for a juvenile court order, unpaid fine or juvenile contempt, or at least two separate traffic convictions within twelve months while under eighteen. Delinquent conduct falls under automatic suspension for those under twenty-one. ALR reinstatement costs $125; triggers include a failed breath or blood test at .08 or above for persons over twenty-one, refusing a test, or detectable alcohol under twenty-one. Cancellation grounds include another state's suspension or revocation, withdrawn parental approval under eighteen, missing required information, ineligibility, incomplete driver education, or false application statements [A12] [A11].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A12
Court orders compel action for child support, interlock, overpayments, incapacity, dependency, or lapsed annual renewal [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A13
Denials track live disqualifications, unsafe conditions, theft, mischief, minor alcohol supply, support debt, unpaid fees, missed court, and drugs, while invalid driving scales from Class C fines through Class B jail to Class A jail with extensions, and skipped traffic court can block renewal [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A13
Zero Tolerance bans all minor alcohol contact, fining first offenses up to five hundred dollars with eight to twelve service hours, courses, and thirty suspended days, seconds with twenty to forty hours and sixty days, thirds at seventeen to twenty reaching Class B and one hundred eighty days without deferred disposition, and under-seventeen thirds at sixty days or juvenile court [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A14
Supplying alcohol to a minor risks four thousand dollars, a year in jail, or both [A14].
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A14
Court-proved essential need buys occupational licenses at ten dollars yearly or twenty for two, the order alone covering forty-five processing days before both order and certified copy ride along, never for commercial rigs [A14].
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0020]
